questions.title: Count Stride-Three Iterations
questions.description:
A loop that steps i = 0, 3, 6, ... while i < n runs ceil(n / 3) times. Count it by simulating the stride loop.

Implement only this function:

    def stride_iterations(n):

It must start i at 0, add 3 per simulated iteration while i < n, and return how many iterations ran.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the iteration count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
count = 0
i = 0
while i < n:
    i += 3
    count += 1
print(count)

questions.title: Count Single Loop Iterations
questions.description:
A single loop "for i in range(n)" runs its body exactly n times. Count the iterations by simulating the loop, not by returning n directly.

Implement only this function:

    def loop_iterations(n):

It must count the iterations of a loop that runs n times (increment a counter once per simulated iteration) and return the count.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the iteration count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
count = 0
for i in range(n):
    count += 1
print(count)

questions.title: Count Nested Loop Iterations
questions.description:
Two fully nested loops "for i in range(n): for j in range(n)" execute the innermost body n * n times. Count it by actually running the nested loop.

Implement only this function:

    def nested_iterations(n):

It must run the simulated nested loops (one counter increment per innermost iteration) and return the total count.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the iteration count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 600

Implement only this function:

    def pair_comparisons(n):

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of comparisons.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000
questions.sourcecode:

print(n * (n - 1) // 2)

questions.title: Doubling Upload Chunks
questions.description:
An uploader sends a large file in chunks of 1, 2, 4, 8, ... MB (each chunk doubles). It stops once a chunk of size >= n MB would be sent — count how many chunk sizes are tried while still smaller than n.

Implement only this function:

    def chunk_steps(n):

It must start a size counter at 1 and double it while it stays strictly below n, returning how many doubling steps ran.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of steps.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000
questions.sourcecode:
n = int(input())
size = 1
steps = 0
while size < n:
    size *= 2
    steps += 1
print(steps)

questions.description:
An announcer repeatedly halves a queue: each announcement splits the current queue in half (floor division), and the process stops when the queue is empty. Count the announcements.

Implement only this function:

    def drop_steps(n):

It must repeatedly replace n with n // 2 while n >= 1 and return how many halvings ran.

Input Format:
One line with the initial queue size.

Output Format:
One line with the announcement count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000
questions.sourcecode:

steps = 0

    steps += 1
print(steps)

questions.title: Classify the Growth Curve
questions.description:
You time an algorithm twice: t1 steps for some input, t2 steps for the doubled input size. Classify the growth: t2 == t1 means constant (return 0), t2 == 2 * t1 means linear (return 1), t2 == 4 * t1 means quadratic (return 2), t2 == t1 + 1 means logarithmic (return 3). Test data always hits exactly one class.

Implement only this function:

    def classify_growth(t1, t2):

It must return 0, 1, 2 or 3 per the rules above (checked in that order).

Input Format:
One line with t1 and t2.

Output Format:
One line with the class number.

Constraints:
1 <= t1 < 1000000, 1 <= t2 < 1000000000

questions.title: Panel Pairwise Visits (No Shortcut)
questions.description:
An interview panel re-interviews: candidate i meets every candidate up to and including themselves (indices 0..i), so candidate 0 has 1 meeting, candidate 1 has 2, and so on. Arithmetic shortcuts are banned — count with real nested loops.

Implement only this function:

    def visit_count(n):

It must run an outer loop i = 0..n-1 and an inner loop j = 0..i, adding 1 to a counter per innermost visit, and return the counter (which equals n * (n + 1) // 2).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the visit count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 800

questions.title: Reshelve Mixed Loop Steps
questions.description:
A library robot drives past each of n carts; for cart i it repeatedly halves the cart's book count (i) until it hits zero, one scan per halving. Count the total scans by simulating the mixed loop (no math shortcuts).

Implement only this function:

    def mixed_count(n):

It must run for i in range(n) an inner while loop that halves i with floor division until it reaches 0, counting one step per halving, and return the total.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total scan count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 5000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def mixed_count(n):
    total = 0
    for i in range(n):
        j = i
        while j > 0:
            j //= 2
            total += 1
    return total


n = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
sys.stdout.write(str(mixed_count(n)) + "\n")

questions.title: Tournament Rounds
questions.description:
A knockout tournament starts with n players. Each round pairs players; with an odd count one player gets a bye, so the next round has ceil(players / 2) = (players + 1) // 2 participants. Count the rounds until one player remains.

Implement only this function:

    def tournament_rounds(n):

It must repeatedly replace the player count with (count + 1) // 2 while count > 1 and return the number of rounds (0 for a single player).

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the number of rounds.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def tournament_rounds(n):
    players = n
    rounds = 0
    while players > 1:
        players = (players + 1) // 2
        rounds += 1
    return rounds


n = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
sys.stdout.write(str(tournament_rounds(n)) + "\n")

questions.title: Linear versus Binary Step Race
questions.description:
On a sorted shelf of n books, linear search needs at most n steps while binary search needs at most the number of halvings of n (floor division until zero). Report both worst-case step counts.

Implement only this function:

    def step_race(n):

It must return the tuple (n, halvings) where halvings counts how many times n can be floor-halved until it reaches 0.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the linear count, then the binary count, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def step_race(n):
    halvings = 0
    m = n
    while m > 0:
        m //= 2
        halvings += 1
    return (n, halvings)


n = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
linear, binary = step_race(n)
sys.stdout.write(str(linear) + " " + str(binary) + "\n")

questions.title: Dynamic Array Copy Count
questions.description:
A dynamic array starts with capacity 1 and doubles its capacity whenever a push would exceed it; every doubling copies all current elements once. Count the total element copies after n pushes (simulate, no math shortcuts).

Implement only this function:

    def copy_count(n):

It must simulate n pushes: before each push, if size equals capacity, add capacity to the copy counter and double capacity; then increment size. Return the copy counter.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total copies.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def copy_count(n):
    capacity = 1
    size = 0
    copies = 0
    for _ in range(n):
        if size == capacity:
            copies += capacity
            capacity *= 2
        size += 1
    return copies


n = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
sys.stdout.write(str(copy_count(n)) + "\n")

questions.title: Item Budget Ceiling
questions.description:
A comparison engine costs 1 unit per unordered pair of items, so n items cost n * (n - 1) / 2 units. Given a budget, find the largest item count whose pairwise cost still fits the budget (1 item always costs 0).

Implement only this function:

    def max_items(budget):

It must return the largest n with n * (n - 1) // 2 <= budget — compute it by incrementally adding n - 1, n - 2, ... to a running cost (simulate with a while loop; no closed-form inversion).

Input Format:
One line with the budget.

Output Format:
One line with the largest item count.

Constraints:
0 <= budget <= 10000000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def max_items(budget):
    n = 1
    total = 0
    while total + n <= budget:
        total += n
        n += 1
    return n


budget = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
sys.stdout.write(str(max_items(budget)) + "\n")

questions.title: Stage Pyramid Blocks
questions.description:
A ceremonial pyramid has n levels; level i (1-based) contains i * (i + 1) / 2 blocks (a triangle of blocks). Count the total blocks by walking the levels with a loop and summing each level's triangular count.

Implement only this function:

    def pyramid_blocks(n):

It must loop i from 1 to n, add i * (i + 1) // 2 per level, and return the total.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total block count.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 1000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def pyramid_blocks(n):
    total = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        total += i * (i + 1) // 2
    return total


n = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
sys.stdout.write(str(pyramid_blocks(n)) + "\n")

questions.title: Even-Divisor Loop Trace
questions.description:
A tracing tool watches this loop nest: for each i from 1 to n it sets j = i and repeatedly floor-halves j while j is even, counting one step per halving. Report the total number of steps (the sum of the powers of two dividing each i).

Implement only this function:

    def even_step_sum(n):

It must simulate the trace exactly as described and return the total step count.

Input Format:
One line with n.

Output Format:
One line with the total steps.

Constraints:
1 <= n <= 10000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def even_step_sum(n):
    total = 0
    for i in range(1, n + 1):
        j = i
        while j % 2 == 0:
            j //= 2
            total += 1
    return total


n = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
sys.stdout.write(str(even_step_sum(n)) + "\n")

questions.title: Viral Message Spread
questions.description:
A forwarded message reaches 1 person at hour 0 and the audience doubles every hour. Report how many hours it takes to reach at least the target audience, and how many extra people beyond the target the final hour delivers.

Implement only this function:

    def spread_report(target):

It must return the tuple (hours, overshoot) where hours counts the doublings until reach >= target and overshoot = final_reach - target.

Input Format:
One line with the target audience.

Output Format:
One line with hours, then the overshoot, space-separated.

Constraints:
1 <= target <= 1000000000
questions.sourcecode:
import sys


def spread_report(target):
    reach = 1
    hours = 0
    while reach < target:
        reach *= 2
        hours += 1
    return (hours, reach - target)


target = int(sys.stdin.read().strip())
hours, overshoot = spread_report(target)
sys.stdout.write(str(hours) + " " + str(overshoot) + "\n")
